title: CI gate 2 (`odin test app`) is flaky: settings tests race on a shared temp path under Odin's parallel test runner, falsifying the 'ci-local 10/10' claim
evidence:
app/settings_test.odin:
// tmp_settings_path — a unique temp path per run (os.temp_dir + a process-
// local counter — hermetic: parallel/CI runs never collide within a binary).
settings_test_seq: u64 // package counter — unique within the test binary

tmp_settings_path :: proc(t: ^testing.T) -> string {
	settings_test_seq += 1

Observed running the exact gate-2 command (`odin test app -out:bin/app-test`, tools/ci-local.sh:56) — 6 of 18 runs failed, different test each time:
settings: no readable settings at /var/folders/.../pp-settings-test-6 — defaults   [printed 6x — six concurrent tests drew the same seq]
settings: /var/folders/.../pp-settings-test-6 has a foreign format — defaults
[ERROR] --- [settings_test.odin:72:settings_foreign_version_defaults()] a foreign-version file must fall back to defaults
Finished 13 tests in 1.362ms. 1 test failed.
 - main.settings_foreign_version_defaults     a foreign-version file must fall back to defaults

Odin's runner is a thread pool (core/testing/runner.odin:377 `thread_count := os.get_processor_core_count()`), so the non-atomic package counter collides and tests clobber each other's fixtures (one failing load read another test's valid-magic file → non-default result).
detail: Briefing AC 2 and PR body demand `tools/ci-local.sh` 10/10; gate 2 fails ~1 run in 3. The r2→r3 claim '13 settings tests' green is unreliable — the delta-0 pin itself flakes.
recommended_fix: Make tmp_settings_path collision-free under concurrency: derive the name from the test identity plus an atomic counter (core:sync), or run these tests serially; re-run gate 2 many times.

title: Python bytecode committed: tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc is tracked in git
evidence:
chunk-rest.patch hunk:
diff --git a/tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc b/tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..f807a4d
Binary files /dev/null and b/tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc differ

Verified in the worktree: `git ls-files tools/__pycache__/` → tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc (tracked). .gitignore gains only `.pp-settings.bin`; no `__pycache__/` entry.
detail: Build detritus, not a spec deliverable; the repo's own hygiene rule is 'never commit binaries' (*.dSYM, bin/, app*.bin are ignored). Stale bytecode can silently diverge from the derivation script.
recommended_fix: git rm --cached the .pyc and add `__pycache__/` to .gitignore in this PR.

title: Spec AC 'scale ×1.50 at 1152×648 — no HUD overlap' is pinned only at 1280×720; the min-window case is untested
evidence:
Frozen spec (spec-7-3-accessibility-core.md, in this diff):
| Scale ×1.50 at min window 1152×648 | panel stepper | top band (health card, forecast, crisis banner), QoS panel, tray, caption strip never overlap | layout clamps, AC-pinned |
- Given scale ×1.50 at 1152×648, then no HUD overlap anywhere (top band, QoS, tray, captions, panel).

The only pin (crisis_card_width_clamp) uses the design resolution:
	v := hud_test_view(1.5)
	v.win_w = 1280
	v.win_h = 720

Repo-wide grep for 1152/648 hits only MIN_WIN_W/MIN_WIN_H in app/main.odin:33-34; the a11y_scale golden renders at 1280×720 (harness view_compute 1280,720).
detail: The frozen AC names 1152×648 and says 'AC-pinned'; no test or golden exercises that size. Horizontal clamp math is win_w-relative so likely holds, but vertical stacking (top band vs QoS/tray/captions) at 648 height is unpinned anywhere.
recommended_fix: Add a hud_test leg at win_w=1152/win_h=648 asserting crisis_card_width clamps and the top-band/QoS/tray/caption rects stay disjoint at ×1.50.
